Reference / http/client

http/client#

An HTTP client.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let client = HttpClient();
let page = await client.get("https://example.com/");
if page::Head::status == Status.ok {
    Stdout().writeln(await page.text());
}
let reply = await client.post(url: "https://api.example.com/orders", body: JsonBody(order));
let created = await reply.json();
client.close();

Description#

An HTTP client.

HttpClient() resolves names with the system's DNS, trusts the system's roots, reaches public endpoints only and speaks HTTP/1.1 with the default limits and timeouts over at most 8 connections; it follows no redirects and keeps no cookies. Each part is replaced by name: HttpClient(endpoints: AllEndpoints(), redirects: Redirects(limit: 5)), HttpClient(cookies: MemoryCookieJar()). Tests and local servers use HttpClient(endpoints: LoopbackEndpoints()).

A response body is read once: whole with bytes(), text() or json(), within the body limit (1 GiB by default), or piece by piece with reading(). Decorators such as Caching, BearerExchanging and Retrying wrap a client and are clients themselves.

Errors#

  • HttpTimeout: the connection, the response head or a pause in the body took too long; phase says which.
  • EndpointDenied: the host resolves only to addresses the client may not reach.
  • ClientClosed: the client was used after close().
  • HttpStaleConnection: a reused connection closed before answering.
